_note: Every long-running arcade service, in one place.
This list used to be written out longhand in five files, and they had drifted:
chat-server.py's status panel knew nothing about Chess or Aggravation,
start-all.sh never started Aggravation at all, admin/server.py had never
heard of Counter, and only the health bot had the full set. Consumers now
read this file instead of keeping their own copy:
arcade/chat-server.py            — status panel (entries with kind 'game')
arcade/start-all.sh              — launches every 'services' entry locally
arcade/scripts/bot-check-services.sh — probes every 'services' entry's port
arcade/admin/server.py           — dashboard cards, and the allowlist of
systemd units it will restart
arcade/scripts/nginx-magmacrunch.conf still spells out its own proxy blocks
(each needs a full stanza), but 'path' here is the name<->port mapping it
must agree with.
TWO ARRAYS, and the difference matters:
'services' is the startable, probeable set. Everything in it takes a --port
argument, gets launched by start-all.sh, and gets a TCP probe from the health
bot every 30 minutes — so an entry here is also an alert path. Adding a game:
add an entry here, an 'icon', a systemd unit in arcade/systemd/, and a
location block in the nginx conf.
'dashboard_only' is for units that exist on the Pi but are neither started
nor probed. Only admin/server.py reads it. arcade-private is here rather than
in 'services' for two reasons, both of which have to be fixed before it could
move: private/server.py takes no --port (it reads config.json), so start-all's
'python3 <exec> --port <port>' would fail argparse and never start it; and
8782 is not proxied by nginx and nothing has confirmed the unit is enabled, so
probing it would create a fresh 'service down' alert that nobody asked for.
Entries here carry no 'dir'/'exec' on purpose — there is nothing to launch.
Not listed at all: admin itself (8780/8781) and mcp (8785). arcade-admin is a
unit the dashboard may restart, but it is hardcoded in admin/server.py, not
read from here — it is the dashboard's own process and is never drawn as a
card. Their units live in arcade/admin/systemd and mcp-server/.
'name' and 'icon' are rendered by the dashboard. admin/server.py rejects the
whole manifest if either contains HTML metacharacters, because its frontend
drops both straight into innerHTML.
